senses.gloss:
homa
(‘pouring oblation’)
------------------------------------------
Vedic sacrifices, which were very simple in the beginning, gradually grew into a labyrinth of rites and rituals. As a reaction to this, in course of time, evolved simpler fire-rituals conducted in the domestic fire. This is how होम was born.
Literally, होम (or हवन) means the act of pouring an oblation (usually of ghee or clarified butter) into a duly consecrated fire. It is an essential feature of domestic rites. Also, it is often considered as an integral part of special पूजा or worship of a deity.
The major steps involved in the performance of a होम are: preparing the स्थण्डिल (altar for the fire, a raised surface of sand or loose earth), purification of the आज्य (ghee used for oblation), warming the ladle, putting the faggots and lighting the fire, pouring of the oblations with mantras appropriate to the deity, पूर्णाहुति (final offering), ceremonially putting out the fire (generally with curds) and preparing the rakṣā (ashes from the remnants pasted with ghee, to be applied on the forehead as a religious mark).
